defects.quote: a Sharpe gap of 2.5 over a year is far above the detectable size for 252 days
defects.evidence: Take two return series correlated 0.6 over 252 days. The standard error of the difference in annualized Sharpe is about √((2−2ρ+½(SR_a²+SR_b²−2ρ²SR_aSR_b))/T)×√252 ≈ 0.90, so a gap of 2.5 is only about 2.8 standard errors. With 18 claims corrected together (Bonferroni two-sided z ≈ 3.0), each claim has roughly 40% power. TC-72 requires all 5 of `topfifth:neural`'s claims to pass on seed 404, so a correct implementation will most likely fail this golden case. The architecture's own Risks line agrees: "12 months of daily returns can only detect a large Sharpe difference".
defects.fix: Re-plant TC-72 so the effect is detectable after correction. For example, use `topfifth:neural` with annualized Sharpe 5.0 against 0.5 at correlation 0.9: the SE of the difference is ≈ 0.45 and the gap is about 10 SE. Alternatively, use `sessions=1260` for the planted seed. Replace the tolerance sentence with the computed margin, and keep the null seeds 405–424 as they are.

defects.quote: and a copy with every bar after 2020-11-30 scaled by 1.5
defects.evidence: The last development date is 2020-11-30 (HOLD-01). Its target is the December 2020 holding-month return (RESID-03), which the development run legitimately reads. Scaling every bar after 2020-11-30 adds a +50% jump on 2020-12-01, so that target changes, and TC-40's "the two development runs write identical `ic`, `gains` and `claims` tables" fails on a correct implementation. Holdout targets start with the 2020-12-31 date, whose holding month is January 2021.
defects.fix: In TC-40, mutate only data after 2020-12-31. Use "a copy with every bar after 2020-12-31 scaled by 1.5 and every return in 2021 onward perturbed", or change the holdout dates' targets directly. Keep the Expected line.

defects.quote: about 69 holdout months detect a mean monthly IC of roughly 0.025 or more
defects.evidence: With an IC spread of 0.10 over 69 dates, the SE of the mean is 0.10/√69 ≈ 0.012. At 80% power and α = 0.05 corrected over the 19-claim family (z ≈ 3.0 + 0.84), the detectable mean IC is ≈ 0.046. Even uncorrected two-sided it is ≈ 0.034. 0.025 overstates the holdout's power, and that number is what the developer will read the verdicts against.
defects.fix: Replace with "about 69 holdout months detect a mean monthly IC of roughly 0.045 or more after the 19-claim correction (≈ 0.034 uncorrected, IC spread 0.10); smaller real effects will read as \"does not pass\"".

defects.quote: then prices up to T equal the unadjusted prices.
defects.evidence: Adjusted prices are compounded back from the anchor through total returns (PRICE-03, AD-06), so any cash dividend between a date t < T and T makes adj(t) ≠ unadjusted(t). docs/architecture.md Risks already notes: "Spec PRICE-03's example … holds only when no dividend falls between those dates and T." The spec was never fixed, and M1-T15 tests against it.
defects.fix: PRICE-03 criterion: "Given a company with a split after date T and no dividend before T, when adjusted prices are requested anchored at T, then prices up to T equal the unadjusted prices." Delete the PRICE-03 bullet from docs/architecture.md Risks.

defects.quote: Given a member with 200 trading days of history on R, when momentum is computed, then it has no value, and reversal, volatility and maximum return do.
defects.evidence: Features are computed only "for every eligible member" (FEAT behaviour), and eligibility needs ≥ 252 returns in the window (STRUCT-02). qrisk TC-13 excludes a 200-day member as "short_history". A 200-day member therefore never gets any feature. The same unreachable case is qfeat TC-30 ("a member with 200 trading days of history on R"), which also expects beta and idiosyncratic volatility to be present.
defects.fix: Restate FEAT-09's example and TC-30 with an eligible member that lacks one lookback. For example: "Given an eligible member whose first return is 252 trading days before R with a 10-day gap inside the window". Alternatively, test momentum's null on a member with < 252 closes before R+21 inside an eligible window, and expect momentum (and volume shock, if short) null while the others are present. Apply in docs/spec.md FEAT-09 and docs/packages/qfeat/tests.md TC-30.
